about.title: What GIEE does
about.body: GIEE connects teachers, researchers, founders and policymakers who want AI in education to be fair and safe. With the Global Online Education Regulator (GOER) and the UN Geneva Forum, we turn what works in real classrooms into benchmarks, policies and guardrails others can adopt.

items.body: Join a live research portfolio, with partners to study, cite and work with.

items.title: I shape policy
items.body: Pick up benchmarks and guardrails that are ready to adapt to your own country.

beliefs.title: What we believe
beliefs.intro: “Human-centred design” is easy to say. These three beliefs are how we hold ourselves to it.

items.title: Technology should make people more capable, never less.
items.body: AI should serve the learner, not the other way round. We check that tools build curiosity, critical thinking and confidence, and don’t gatekeep, shrink or replace the human side of learning.

items.title: Fairness has to be designed in.
items.body: Nobody stumbles into ethical AI. Before a tool reaches millions of learners, someone has to check how it treats their privacy, their access and their wellbeing. We make that check part of the process.

items.title: Trust decides whether any of it works.
items.body: If teachers, students and families can’t trust the tools they rely on, even good ideas fail. Open, careful governance turns that doubt into shared progress.

caseStudies.name: Women in AI Framework
caseStudies.summary: Bringing women’s perspectives into every stage of how AI gets made.
caseStudies.description: How can women’s perspectives shape AI at every stage, from the first idea to everyday use? This initiative looks at how to build that in, structurally.
partners: Mount Saint Mary’s University (Los Angeles, CA)
University of Barcelona — Social Work Department

caseStudies.name: Insight Recognition
caseStudies.summary: AI-supported assessment that maps what each learner knows, from the bottom up.
caseStudies.description: An AI-driven assessment and personalised learning space that maps what each person knows, through their own, bottom-up concept maps.

caseStudies.name: Scaling & Expanding Youth-Led Critical AI Education
caseStudies.summary: AI programmes co-designed with young people, and training for the teachers who run them.
caseStudies.description: GLITCH (Generating Liberation through Intersectionality, Technology and Critical Hope) is a research lab building fair, community-centred AI programmes for young people from under-resourced communities. Co-designing with youth, it also creates training for teachers who want more just and joyful ways to bring AI into class.
partners: Center for Resilience and Digital Justice (UCLA)
Community Health Informatics Data Lab (Brown University)

caseStudies.name: murmur: AI Design in Mental Health
caseStudies.summary: A clinician-supervised tool, built on Schema Therapy, that gives learners room to reflect.
caseStudies.description: A structured clinical tool, built on Schema Therapy models, that gives learners space for reflection, always with a clinician supervising.

caseStudies.name: Street Racket: Schools and Hybrid Learning Environments
caseStudies.summary: How learning through movement grows with AI-supported reflection and goal-setting.
caseStudies.description: How can learning through movement grow with AI-supported reflection and goal-setting? This study finds out, on court and in class.

caseStudies.name: CheckIT Learning: AI Supporting SEN Students
caseStudies.summary: Responsible AI, grounded in the science of learning, for students with special educational needs.
caseStudies.description: How can responsible AI, grounded in the science of learning, improve outcomes for students with special educational needs (SEN)? The study looks at how student partnership, teacher learning and shared governance make education more inclusive.

caseStudies.name: Flowwwly: From Screen Dependency to Purpose
caseStudies.summary: A human-centred app that helps young people trade screen time for purpose and real-world action.
caseStudies.description: Too much screen time, too little sense of purpose: this study looks at how Flowwwly combines purpose discovery, AI-supported guidance and real-world challenges to help young people build healthier habits and get involved in things that matter to them.
